exclusion_detail: Lead 10b (picomolar fluorine-bearing compound, the abstract's best affinity) needs 6 reactions: benzoxazinone from 2-amino-5-bromobenzoic acid + 2-fluorobenzoyl chloride (6), ring opening with (R)-1-Boc-3-(aminomethyl)piperidine (7), LiOH/ethylene glycol cyclisation to quinazolinone (8), Cu-catalysed Ullmann ether with 6-hydroxybenzothiazole, Boc removal (9b), N-isopropylation (10b).

lead.label: 10b
lead.why: Abstract: 'one fluorine-bearing compound (10b) with picomolar binding affinity (20 pM), representing the highest binding affinity for GHS-R1a reported to date'; the Results call it 'the best candidate for developing into a radiotracer'.

notes: Abstract also names 5b and 5e as 'lead compounds' that were 18F-radiolabelled, and 5i and 17 as subnanomolar. 10b was taken as the lead because it is the 'best' compound named; 5b/5e are radiolabelling precursors/leads (radiochemistry would also be out of scope). All final compounds need at least 5 steps (3 for the quinazolinone core, Ullmann, Boc removal), so none qualifies under the 4-step limit. 10c needs 6 as well.
